key_insight: An explainable machine-learning model, especially calibrated Extreme Gradient Boosting, can predict cervical cancer screening use in Ethiopian women with high accuracy and highlight who is most likely to be missed.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help public health teams target outreach and primary-care screening invitations to women at highest risk of not being screened, supporting cervical cancer prevention efforts.
method: Analyzed 2024–2025 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey data from women aged 15–49
Compared six supervised models, including logistic regression, decision tree, random forest, gradient boosting, and XGBoost
Used SMOTE for class imbalance, isotonic calibration, and SHAP to interpret drivers
evidence_signal: XGBoost performed best with AUROC 0.896 and AUPRC 0.781, and calibration improved the Brier score to 0.038 with net benefit across 5%–55% decision thresholds.
watch_item: This is a model-development study on survey data, so performance may drop in real-world settings without external validation, workflow integration, and careful handling of equity and data quality.
paper_title: Predicting Cervical Cancer Screening Utilization Among Women of Reproductive Age in Ethiopia Using Supervised Machine Learning: A Nationally Representative 2024/25 EDHS Study
